temporal · event-time axis
Q: Who did I go with to the music event last Saturday?
gold answer: my parents
NoOrg · incorrect
You went to the music event last Saturday (April 15, 2023) with a group of
friends — specifically mentioned in the memory entry from 2023/04/01:
I just got back from a music festival in Brooklyn with a group of friends,
featuring a lineup of my favorite indie bands.”
While the April 15 entry (“I'm also interested in discovering new artists… I
recently attended a music festival in Brooklyn…”) doesn’t restate the
companions, it refers to the same Brooklyn music festival previously described
— and all prior references to that festival consistently specify you attended
with a group of friends.
So, the answer is: a group of friends.
VAULT · correct
Last Saturday was April 15, 2023 — and based on your memory entry from that
date, you went to the Queen concert with your parents at the Prudential Center
in Newark, NJ.
So, you went with your parents.
why it flips
flips because the event-time axis resolves “last Saturday” to 04/15 — NoOrg picked the wrong music event (04/01 festival) and its companion
knowledge-update · supersede
Q: How many free night's stays can I redeem at any Hilton property with my accumulated points?
gold answer: two
NoOrg · incorrect
Based on the memory entries, you’ve stated:
I've accumulated enough points for a single free night's stay at any Hilton
property.”
and
I've accumulated enough points for a single free night's stay at any Hilton
property... Since Hilton Lake Las Vegas Resort is a Category 5 hotel, I'm good
to redeem my points for a weekend getaway.”
You also confirmed having “enough points for a single free night’s stay” — and
later, in the context of the Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower (a Category 7
property), you were noted to have “enough points for two free nights” — but
that appears to be a separate, later scenario (from 2023/05/30) and is not
consistent with your original statement from 2023/05/29.
Crucially, no specific point balance was ever disclosed, and the number of
free nights depends entirely on:
- Your total accumulated Hilton Honors points,
- The category (and peak/off-peak status) of the hotel(s) you wish to book.
However, your own explicit statement on 2023/05/29 — repeated verbatim twice —
is definitive:
I've accumulated enough points for a single free night's stay at any Hilton
property.”
Therefore, you can redeem exactly one free night’s stay — assuming standard
redemption (e.g., ~40,000–50,000 points for a Category 5 like Hilton Lake Las
Vegas, or up to ~60,000 for a Category 7 like Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower,
depending on date/availability). This implies your point balance covers at
least the minimum requirement for one standard reward night across most
categories — but not more than one.
So, the answer is:
You can redeem one free night’s stay at any Hilton property with your
currently accumulated points.
VAULT · correct
Based on the memory entries, you have accumulated enough points for two free
night’s stays at any Hilton property.
This is explicitly confirmed in the entry from 2023/05/30 (Tue) 12:28:
By the way, I've accumulated enough points for two free night's stays at any
Hilton property, so I might use that for a separate trip to Las Vegas.”
Additionally, earlier on 2023/05/29, it was noted you had enough for “a single
free night’s stay” — but the later and more recent statement (and contextually
consistent with your planning of both a Paris trip and a Las Vegas trip)
clarifies the updated total: two free nights.
So, the answer is:
You can redeem your accumulated Hilton Honors points for two free night stays,
subject to hotel category, date availability, and peak/off-peak pricing. For
example:
- At a Category 5 hotel (e.g., Hilton Lake Las Vegas Resort), ~40,000–50,000
points/night → two nights would require ~80,000–100,000 points total.
- At a Category 7 hotel (e.g., Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower), ~50,000–60,000
points/night → two nights would require ~100,000–120,000 points total.
- At a Category 10 luxury property (e.g., Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas),
~90,000–120,000 points/night → two nights would require up to ~240,000 points.
Let me know if you'd like help checking availability or estimating points
needed for specific dates/hotels!
why it flips
flips because supersede filters the outdated “one night” claim before the reader sees it — the newer “two nights” wins by default
multi-session · associative graph
Q: How much cashback did I earn at SaveMart last Thursday?
gold answer: $0.75
NoOrg · incorrect
You did not earn any cashback at SaveMart last Thursday — the $75 grocery
expense you reported was simply tracked as an expense for budgeting purposes,
and none of the memory entries indicate that you earned or claimed cashback
(e.g., via SaveMart’s loyalty program, Ibotta, Fetch Rewards, or another
platform) on that transaction.
The only cashback discussions in your history relate to:
- SaveMart’s 1% cashback for members (mentioned on 2023/05/22), but you didn’t
confirm whether you applied it to the $75 purchase;
- Walmart+’s 2% cashback (on Walmart online groceries, not SaveMart);
- Ibotta and Fetch Rewards (general usage noted, but no linkage to the
SaveMart $75 spend).
So unless you later confirmed using SaveMart’s 1% cashback (or another
cashback method) on that $75 purchase — which isn’t recorded in the provided
memories — $0 cashback is reflected for that transaction.
Let me know if you’d like help calculating potential cashback (e.g., 1% of $75
= $0.75) or tracking future rewards!
VAULT · correct
Based on the memory entries, you spent $75 on groceries at SaveMart last
Thursday (which, given the current date of 2023/05/30 and the context, was
Thursday, May 25).
You mentioned having a SaveMart membership that earns 1% cashback on all
purchases, as confirmed in the May 22 conversation:
I have a membership there and can earn 1% cashback on all purchases."
...with 1% cashback, you'll earn $0.01 for every dollar you spend at
SaveMart."
So, for the $75 purchase:
You earned $0.75 in cashback at SaveMart last Thursday.
why it flips
flips because the associative edge pulls the $75 expense and the 1% cashback terms from two different sessions into one top-10
three of 78 questions flipped by offline organization (McNemar net +50, p ≈ 1.3e-6, replicated under two judges)
